front_matter.title: The tower's pairing gap at fixed charges is twice the quasiparticle energy

extraction.note: The problem's second line of attack (fluctuations of the tower's composite scalars beyond mean field), taken from outside the series: top condensation (Bardeen, Hill and Lindner) and the Nambu relation m_sigma = 2m of the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model. The stored pairing element H_4 is the degenerate (single-shell) pairing model; its exact spectrum is the quasi-spin (seniority) spectrum (Kerman 1961, imported in synthesis.imported-quasi-spin-pairing-and-top-condensation), certified here exactly on all sectors of the n_b = 2, 3 floors at eight (K, G). At equal numbers the first excitation above the band breaks a pair and costs exactly G n_b, which is twice the mean-field quasiparticle energy E = G n_b/2: the pair-breaking (two-quasiparticle) threshold, 2E >= 2 Delta, equal to 2 Delta on the shell K = 0. The uniform scalar channel does not reach it on a floor, so its relation to Nambu's m_sigma = 2m is an analogy (argued). Outside comparison (imported, the same Fact; arXiv 1906.09579): in the one-doublet top-condensation model the large-N_c relation is m_chi = 2 m_t, about sqrt(2) m_t with gauge and Higgs corrections, both too large for 125 GeV; the same paper gets a light composite Higgs from two condensates (mostly b-bbar with a top admixture), the several-species case. The record comparison is conditional on reading the rung field's neutral mode as lying at or above this threshold; the rung field is a doublet, the composite a single complex scalar, so the reading is a test, not a construction. Standard content re-derived in the formalism; transport-absent.

levels.formal:
Let $H_{4} = \sum_{b}K(n_{a} + n_{c}) - G\,P^{*}P$, $P = \sum_{b}w_{a}w_{c}$, be the pairing element of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.composite-scalars-mean-field-level}(2) on a floor with $n_{b}$ blocks, $K \ge 0$, $G > 0$, acting on the Fock space of its $2n_{b}$ tower modes (the tower planes generate the CAR, Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit}).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Closed spectrum.)} $H_{4}$ conserves $N_{a}$ and $N_{c}$. In the sector $(N_{a}, N_{c})$ its eigenvalues are exactly the numbers $K(2p + s_{a} + s_{c}) - G(j + j_{z})(j - j_{z} + 1)$, where $s_{a}$ blocks hold $a$ alone, $s_{c}$ blocks hold $c$ alone, $p = N_{a} - s_{a} = N_{c} - s_{c}$ pairs occupy the remaining $\Omega = n_{b} - s_{a} - s_{c}$ blocks, $j_{z} = p - \Omega/2$, and $j \in \{\Omega/2, \Omega/2 - 1, \dots\}$ with $j \ge |j_{z}|$. The stored pair band $2Kn - Gn(n_{b} - n + 1)$ is $s_{a} = s_{c} = 0$, $j = n_{b}/2$, and is the lowest level of the sector $N_{a} = N_{c} = n$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Gap at fixed numbers.)} For $N_{a} = N_{c} = n$ with $0 < n < n_{b}$, the next level lies exactly $Gn_{b}$ above the band level, for every $K$ and $n$: breaking one pair, or lowering the quasi-spin by one, costs $Gn_{b}$, and no level lies between. This level is the pair-breaking (two-quasiparticle) threshold; the uniform scalar channel $P + P^{*}$ moves only along the band and does not reach it.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Twice the quasiparticle energy.)} Above the threshold $G > 2K/n_{b}$ the one-shell mean-field energy $n_{b}(K - E) + \Delta^{2}/G$, $E^{2} = K^{2} + \Delta^{2}$, is stationary and convex exactly at $E = Gn_{b}/2$, the gap equation, so the exact gap of (ii) is $Gn_{b} = 2E = 2\sqrt{K^{2} + \Delta^{2}}$ with $\Delta$ the mean-field fermion mass: the pair-breaking threshold sits at twice the quasiparticle energy, at least $2\Delta$, and at exactly $2\Delta$ when $K = 0$, the floor analogue of Nambu's relation $m_{\sigma} = 2m$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Reading the rung field as such a composite.)} If the rung field's neutral mode is read as a tower composite of one fermion species of mean-field mass $m_{f} = \Delta$, lying at or above the pair-breaking threshold, then $m_{h} \ge 2m_{f}$ at this level. With the measured $m_{h}$ this needs $m_{f} < 63$ GeV, and with the tree value $m_{h} = M_{Z}$ of the D-term action (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-d-term-action-and-tree-masses-on-the-lift-locus}) $m_{f} < 46$ GeV; both exclude the top quark as sole constituent at this level (one species, single shell), since $2m_{t}$ exceeds both. Composites of several species, or mixing between condensates, are not excluded.
\end{enumerate}
levels.technical:
The stored composite scalars of the tower are built at mean field. Beyond mean field the pairing element on a floor is the degenerate pairing model, whose exact spectrum is the quasi-spin spectrum: in each sector of fixed numbers $N_{a}, N_{c}$ the levels are $K(2p + s) - G(j + j_{z})(j - j_{z} + 1)$, with $s$ singly occupied blocks, $p$ pairs on the others, quasi-spin $j$ and projection $j_{z}$. At equal numbers the band of the stored result is the lowest level and the next lies exactly $Gn_{b}$ above it: the pair-breaking (two-quasiparticle) threshold, which the uniform scalar channel does not reach on a floor.

The mean-field gap equation puts the quasiparticle energy at $E = Gn_{b}/2$, so the exact gap is $2E = 2\sqrt{K^{2} + \Delta^{2}}$, at least twice the fermion mass $\Delta$: by analogy, the floor form of Nambu's relation $m_{\sigma} = 2m$. If the Higgs boson is read as a composite of one species lying at or above this threshold, that species must be lighter than $m_{h}/2$, about $63$ GeV, or $M_{Z}/2$ at the tree level of the D-term action, which excludes the top quark as sole constituent at this level (one species, single shell). Light composites from several condensates, as in two-condensate models of top and bottom pairing, are not covered.
levels.lay:
In this framework a scalar particle can arise as a bound pair of fermions, but so far only in an averaged approximation. This result solves the underlying model exactly on finite pieces of it. The lowest way to disturb the paired state without changing the particle numbers is to break one pair, and that costs exactly twice the energy of one dressed fermion, as the averaged treatment predicts.

By analogy with the known relation for such models, a composite scalar of this kind would weigh at least twice its constituents. If the Higgs boson were such a pair of a single kind of fermion, those fermions would have to be lighter than half its mass, about 63 GeV. The top quark is far heavier, so in this simple setting the Higgs cannot be a pair of top quarks alone, in line with the known difficulty of top-quark condensation; pairs mixing several kinds of fermion are not ruled out.
levels.one-liner: Beyond mean field the tower's pairing element has the closed quasi-spin spectrum on every floor, and at fixed numbers its first excitation, the pair-breaking threshold, lies exactly $Gn_{b} = 2E = 2\sqrt{K^{2} + \Delta^{2}}$ above the pair band; by analogy with Nambu's relation, a rung field read as a one-species composite at or above that threshold excludes the top quark as sole constituent at this level.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i).} The element is that of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.composite-scalars-mean-field-level}(2), on the Fock space of the floor's tower modes, which generate the CAR (Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit}). $H_{4}$ is a sum of number operators and of $P^{*}P = \sum_{b,b'}v_{c}(b)v_{a}(b)w_{a}(b')w_{c}(b')$ (with $v$ creating, as in the stored check), which moves a complete pair from block $b'$ to block $b$; so it conserves $N_{a}$ and $N_{c}$, and it annihilates any state in which block $b'$ holds $a$ or $c$ alone, while such a block cannot receive a pair. A block holding one particle alone is therefore inert for the pairing term and contributes $K$. On the remaining $\Omega$ blocks, each empty or paired, the operators $P$, $P^{*}$ and $p - \Omega/2$ close on $\mathfrak{su}(2)$: with $J_{+} = P^{*}$, $J_{-} = P$ restricted to these blocks and $J_{z} = p - \Omega/2$, each block is a quasi-spin $\tfrac12$ (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.how-close-tower-comes-ccr} is the same algebra on a whole floor), and $P^{*}P = J_{+}J_{-} = J^{2} - J_{z}^{2} + J_{z} = (j + j_{z})(j - j_{z} + 1)$ on total quasi-spin $j$, with $j_{z}$ the eigenvalue of $J_{z}$. The total quasi-spin of $\Omega$ spins $\tfrac12$ takes the values $\Omega/2, \Omega/2 - 1, \dots$, and the kinetic term is $K$ times the particle number $2p + s_{a} + s_{c}$. This is the quasi-spin (seniority) solution of the degenerate pairing model (Kerman, 1961; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-quasi-spin-pairing-and-top-condensation}(i)). The check does not rely on it: it builds $H_{4}$ on the full Fock space of the $n_{b} = 2, 3$ floors with GA's exterior model of the CAR (creation by wedge, annihilation by contraction), and in every sector $(N_{a}, N_{c})$, at eight couples $(K, G)$ including $K = 0$ and couplings on both sides of the threshold, verifies exactly that the product of $H_{4} - E$ over the predicted values vanishes on the sector (every eigenvalue is predicted) and that the product over all but one predicted value does not (every predicted value occurs), and that the lowest predicted value at $N_{a} = N_{c} = n$ is the stored band value. For $G > 0$ the energy decreases with $j$ at fixed $j_{z}$, so the band ($j = n_{b}/2$, no inert block) is the lowest level of its sector; a blocked pair of blocks lowers the available quasi-spin by one, as does a lower $j$, and higher seniorities cost more.

\emph{(ii).} At $N_{a} = N_{c} = n$, $0 < n < n_{b}$, the band level is $2Kn - Gn(n_{b} - n + 1)$. The next candidates have the same particle number and quasi-spin lowered by one: either $s_{a} = s_{c} = 1$ with $n - 1$ pairs on $n_{b} - 2$ blocks at top quasi-spin, or no inert block and $j = n_{b}/2 - 1$; both give $2Kn - G(n - 1)(n_{b} - n)$. The difference is $G[n(n_{b} - n + 1) - (n - 1)(n_{b} - n)] = Gn_{b}$, independent of $n$ and $K$. By (i) no other value lies between (the check confirms the two lowest predicted values differ by exactly $Gn_{b}$ in every such sector and that both occur).

\emph{(iii).} The one-shell mean-field energy of the stored result is $f(x) = n_{b}(K - \sqrt{K^{2} + x}) + x/G$ with $x = \Delta^{2}$; $f'(x) = -n_{b}/(2\sqrt{K^{2} + x}) + 1/G$ vanishes exactly at $\sqrt{K^{2} + x} = Gn_{b}/2$, which is positive-$x$ exactly when $G > 2K/n_{b}$ (the stored threshold), and $f''(x) = n_{b}/(4(K^{2} + x)^{3/2}) > 0$. So the mean-field quasiparticle energy is $E = Gn_{b}/2$ and $Gn_{b} = 2E = 2\sqrt{K^{2} + \Delta^{2}} \ge 2\Delta$, with equality exactly at $K = 0$, $\Delta$ being the mean-field fermion mass. Checked exactly at four above-threshold samples with rational $E$ and $\Delta$, one with $K = 0$. On a single shell the uniform scalar channel $P + P^{*}$ moves only along the band, so the level at $2E$ is the pair-breaking (two-quasiparticle) threshold and is not reached by the composite-scalar operator on a floor. Its relation to the amplitude mode of the relativistic model, where many shells are present and the bound state sits at $2m$ (Nambu and Jona-Lasinio; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-quasi-spin-pairing-and-top-condensation}(ii)), is an analogy (argued): the threshold is the floor's counterpart of the energy at which that mode sits, not the mode itself.

\emph{(iv).} Under the reading stated, with the neutral mode at or above the pair-breaking threshold, $m_{h} \ge 2E \ge 2m_{f}$, $m_{f} = \Delta$ the constituent's mean-field mass. The stored $m_{h} = 125.20$ GeV gives $m_{f} \le 62.6$ GeV and the stored $M_{Z} = 91.188$ GeV, the tree value of $m_{h}$ in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-d-term-action-and-tree-masses-on-the-lift-locus}, gives $m_{f} \le 45.6$ GeV; the stored $m_{t} = 172.57$ GeV exceeds both bounds (checked exactly), so the top quark is excluded as the sole constituent at this level (one species, single shell). For comparison (outside; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-quasi-spin-pairing-and-top-condensation}(iii), arXiv 1906.09579, which cites the large-$N_{c}$ result): in the minimal top-condensation model the composite Higgs has $m_{\chi} = 2m_{t}$ at large $N_{c}$ and about $\sqrt{2}\,m_{t}$ with gauge and Higgs corrections, both too large. The same paper obtains its own light composite Higgs, about $125$ GeV, from two condensates (mostly bottom-antibottom with a top admixture, through axial $U(1)$ breaking), which is the several-species case left open here. The floor result supplies the analogue of the first relation inside the series. Limits of the reading: the rung field is a doublet with a charged pair, the composite here a single complex scalar of one shell; colour, gauge corrections and the running between the cutoff and the weak scale are absent; the bound concerns a composite of one species, and a composite of several species, or mixing between condensates, is not excluded by this computation.
